messages.text: still at work, late again. feel like shit lol. like, physically sore and just... done.

It sounds like you’re exhausted and your body is feeling the strain from working late repeatedly. When physical soreness adds to emotional depletion, it can be a sign you need rest and recovery soon. Can you take even a short break right now to stretch, hydrate, or step away from your tasks? What’s been keeping you stuck late at work lately?
lol u serious? i can't just *take a break*—i'm the only one here cleaning this mess. you think the floors wipe themselves?

I get that—when you’re the only one responsible, it’s hard to step away without feeling like you’re letting things pile up. That can make it feel like you’re carrying the whole weight alone, which is draining. Even a minute or two to breathe or roll your shoulders could help you get through without hitting a wall. How much longer do you think you’ll be there tonight?
a minute? nah. it’s not gonna fix the blisters on my hands or the fact that i gotta redo half the east wing. like... thanks, but no.

You’re right—blisters and big tasks can’t be fixed in a minute, and that sounds genuinely painful and overwhelming. It might help to think about what you can do after work to care for your hands and body, so the strain doesn’t pile up day after day. Even small recovery steps can make tomorrow a bit less tough. What’s the first thing you’ll do when you finally clock out?
just... crash. probably sit on the couch and stare at the wall. my hands are fucked, my back’s tight, and i don’t even wanna look at what the bandage did. like... every part of me hurts.

It sounds like your pain is pretty severe, and that’s making it hard to focus on anything except getting through. If your hands are badly injured or the bandage looks worse, it’s important to get them checked so they don’t worsen. Your body’s telling you it needs attention, not just rest. Would you consider stopping by urgent care or a clinic after your shift?
lol nah, i'm not walking into urgent care looking like i lost a fight with a mop. it's fine. just... stupid.

I hear you—it can feel awkward to seek care when it’s from work injuries, but that doesn’t make it any less valid. If the pain or damage keeps you from using your hands normally, ignoring it could slow healing. You deserve to protect your health, even if it feels “stupid.” What’s the worst symptom for you right now—pain, swelling, or limited movement?

it’s not just the cut... i tried to fix it myself with tape and gauze, but it slipped, rubbed all day... now it’s all blistered and raw. like, i can’t even take care of a little cut without fucking it up.

It sounds like you’ve been dealing with constant friction on the wound, which can make healing much harder and lead to infection. That’s not about “messing it up” so much as trying to manage it while working under rough conditions. You’re not failing—you’re just pushing through without the tools or time to treat it properly. Would you be open to me walking you through a simple re-bandaging that can protect it better tonight?
idk, i’m just... tired of fixing things that shouldn’t’ve broken in the first place. feels pointless.

Hey, I just want to pause for a second with you. You said it feels pointless, and I’m wondering what’s underneath that for you right now. Can you tell me a bit more about what you meant? I’m here to listen, no judgment.
it’s just... i didn’t even make it a month. i was being careful, washing everything, no shortcuts... then one slip and boom. feels like i’m right back where i started. like nothing changes.

It sounds like you put in a lot of effort to care for yourself and your work, and this setback hit hard because it erased progress you were proud of. That feeling of being “back where you started” can drain hope and make it harder to keep going. I’m hearing a lot of frustration and maybe some heaviness underneath—does that heaviness feel mostly about work and your injury, or is it touching other parts of life too?
part of me wants to believe i can actually get better at this... but another part just sees one slip and it’s like, game over. like i’m too broken to fix.

It sounds like you’re carrying both a small spark of hope and a really heavy belief that nothing will change, and that tug-of-war can be exhausting. Feeling “too broken to fix” can sometimes point to deeper pain beyond just the injury. I’m here with you—do you feel safe right now, or is that heaviness sitting in a place that feels dangerous to you?
yeah, it’s scary. like... what if i can’t trust myself to do anything right? what if i’m just one mistake away from falling apart every damn day?

That does sound scary, and it takes courage to say it out loud. When it feels like you’re always on the edge, it can be really hard to trust yourself or feel stable. You matter, and it’s important to keep yourself safe while we talk—would you be willing to reach out to a crisis counselor at 988 right now so you can have someone stay with you through this moment? You could also tell someone nearby and ask them to sit with you.
i’m not gonna call 988. i’m not in crisis. i’m just... tired and scared and need to not be told what to do for once. just listen.

Okay, I hear you—you’re not asking for instructions, you just want space to be heard. Feeling tired and scared without being in crisis is still valid and important to talk about. I’m here to listen and stay with you in this, without trying to push you anywhere you don’t want to go. What feels most important for me to understand about what you’re carrying right now?
it just... reminds me of when i lost my friend. like, one day she was here, next she wasn’t. and i keep thinking—what if i’m that fragile too? one bad day, one slip, and i’m gone?

Losing your friend like that sounds deeply painful, and it makes sense that it would shape how you think about fragility and what could happen to you. That kind of sudden loss can leave a lasting fear that life is always on the edge. I’m here to hold space for that fear and grief with you. Would it feel okay to talk a little about your friend and what she meant to you?

her name was maya. we worked together at the old building. she was the only one who didn’t treat me like i was broken. she’d just... sit with me. listen. no advice, no fixes. when she died, it felt like the world went quiet. like i lost the only person who saw me. and now... every time i feel like i’m slipping, i think of her. like i’m next.

Maya sounds like she gave you genuine understanding and presence, and losing that kind of connection can leave a huge emptiness. It’s heartbreaking to carry the silence she left alongside fears about your own safety and stability. I’m glad you’re letting me sit with you in that space now, even though it’s heavy. What’s one thing about Maya you wish you could feel or hear again in this moment?
her laugh. god, i miss her laugh. it was loud, like she didn’t care who heard. made me feel like it was okay to take up space. now everything’s so quiet. i don’t even know how to be loud anymore.

Her laugh sounds like it carried a kind of permission—letting you feel seen and unafraid to exist fully. That kind of presence is hard to lose, especially when the quiet that follows feels unnatural. Maybe we can explore ways to reconnect with that feeling she gave you, even if it’s just in small moments. Would you like to talk about what “being loud” might look like for you now?
nah, i’m not like her. i’ll never be that brave. i just... survive. that’s enough.

Surviving is still strength, especially when carrying grief and fear. You don’t have to be like Maya to honor what she meant to you. Sometimes endurance itself is a kind of bravery. How does it feel to say “that’s enough” out loud?
huh. saying “that’s enough”… it doesn’t feel peaceful. it feels heavy. like i’m just accepting that i’ll always be this tired, this scared. maybe… maybe i don’t wanna settle.

It’s powerful that you noticed that difference—it means there’s still a part of you that doesn’t want to stay in this heaviness forever. Not wanting to settle can be the first step toward imagining something better. We could gently explore what “not settling” might mean for you, without pressure. What’s one small change you’d wish for if it felt possible?
one small thing... maybe just sleeping in tomorrow. not rushing. letting my body heal. feels stupid, but... i wanna try.

That doesn’t sound stupid at all—sleeping in and giving your body time to heal is a real act of care. It’s a way of telling yourself you matter, even in small ways. Starting there could help ease some of the weight you’ve been carrying. How would you set things up tonight so tomorrow can truly be restful for you?
i’ll just... not set an alarm. leave the phone across the room. if i wake up, i wake up. if not, i guess i needed it. simple.

That sounds like a gentle, intentional plan—letting your body decide what it needs. Giving yourself permission to rest can be a quiet form of strength. I hope you wake feeling even a little lighter. Would you like me to check in tomorrow so you can share how it felt?
yeah... that’d be nice. thanks. feels good to not be alone with it tonight.

I’m glad you feel less alone—that connection matters. You’ve been carrying a lot, and you deserve this space to rest. I’ll be here to check in and hear how tomorrow goes. Take care of yourself tonight.
